problem: A plate of mass $M$ occupies region bounded by two circles ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1$ and ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4.$ Its mass density at any point is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{3}{14\pi }M\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $x$-axis.
worked_solution:
For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D={(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le 2,\,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi }.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{3}{14\pi }Mr.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3}{14\pi }M{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{4}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }({\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{4}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }\cdot \frac{1}{5}{r}^{5}{|}_{1}^{2}\cdot ({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta )}{2}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }\cdot \frac{31}{5}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}\theta -\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }\cdot \frac{31}{5}\cdot \pi  \\  & =\frac{93M}{70}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{x} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{93M}{70}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{93}{70}}.\end{aligned}
$$
